sections.title: Section I
sections.instructions: Attempt Questions 1 to 10. Allow about 15 minutes for this section.

sampleAnswer.t: $\cos^{2} 3x = \tfrac12\left(1 + \cos 6x\right)$, so the integral is $\left[\dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{\sin 6x}{12}\right]_0^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}} = - \dfrac{1}{12} + \dfrac{\pi}{8}$.

classification.content: Integrals of sin squared and cos squared

stem.t: How many subsets of $\{1, 2, 3, \ldots, 14\}$ have exactly 5 elements, no two of which are consecutive integers?

sampleAnswer.t: Write the chosen numbers as $a_1 < a_2 < \cdots < a_{5}$ and let $b_i = a_i - (i - 1)$. The condition $a_{i+1} \ge a_i + 2$ becomes $b_{i+1} > b_i$, and the $b_i$ are any 5 different numbers from $1$ to $10$. So there are $\dbinom{10}{5} = 252$ subsets.

classification.content: Combinations; choosing with gaps

stem.t: Let $\underset{\sim}{a} = -\underset{\sim}{i} - 4\underset{\sim}{j}$ and $\underset{\sim}{b} = 4\underset{\sim}{i} + 3\underset{\sim}{j}$. What is the projection of $\underset{\sim}{a}$ onto $\underset{\sim}{b}$?

sampleAnswer.t: $\mathrm{proj}_{\underset{\sim}{b}}\underset{\sim}{a} = \dfrac{\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}}{\underset{\sim}{b}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}}\underset{\sim}{b} = \dfrac{-16}{25}\underset{\sim}{b} = -\dfrac{64}{25}\underset{\sim}{i} - \dfrac{48}{25}\underset{\sim}{j}$.

classification.content: Projection of vectors

stem.t: The graph of $y = f(x)$ is shown.

sampleAnswer.t: For $x \ge 0$ the graph of $y = f(|x|)$ is the same as that of $y = f(x)$, and the part for $x < 0$ is its reflection in the $y$-axis. Only graph D has this form.

classification.content: Graphs of y = f(|x|) and related functions

stem.t: When the polynomial $P(x)$ is divided by $x - 1$ the remainder is $-6$, and when it is divided by $x - 3$ the remainder is $-7$.
What is the remainder when $P(x)$ is divided by $(x - 1)(x - 3)$?

sampleAnswer.t: The remainder has the form $mx + c$, and $P(x) = (x - 1)(x - 3)Q(x) + mx + c$. Then $P(1) = -6$ and $P(3) = -7$ give $m + c = -6$ and $3m + c = -7$, so $m = - \dfrac{1}{2}$ and $c = - \dfrac{11}{2}$.

classification.content: Remainder theorem; division by a quadratic

stem.t: Which differential equation could have the slope field shown?

sampleAnswer.t: At $(0, -2)$ the slope in the field is about $4$, which matches $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y^2 - x$ (the other equations give $0, 0, 0$ there).

classification.content: Slope fields

stem.t: What is the least number of whole numbers needed to guarantee that at least three of them leave the same remainder when divided by 9?

sampleAnswer.t: There are 9 possible remainders. With $2 \times 9 = 18$ objects it is possible to have exactly 2 in each, so no three share. With one more, by the pigeonhole principle some remainders must contain at least 3. So the answer is $19$.

classification.content: Pigeonhole principle

stem.t: The tangent to the curve $y = 3x^{4}$ at the point where $x = 2$ meets the $x$-axis at $P$.

sampleAnswer.t: At $x = 2$ the gradient is $3 \times 4 \times 2^{3}$ and $y = 3 \times 2^{4}$. The tangent meets $y = 0$ where $x = 2 - \dfrac{y}{y'} = 2 - \dfrac{2}{4} = \dfrac{3}{2}$.

classification.content: Tangents; derivatives of powers and exponentials

stem.t: The polynomial $P(x) = 2 x^{3} + 2 x^{2} + 6 x - 9$ has zeros $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$. What is the value of $\dfrac{1}{\alpha} + \dfrac{1}{\beta} + \dfrac{1}{\gamma}$?

sampleAnswer.t: $\dfrac{1}{\alpha} + \dfrac{1}{\beta} + \dfrac{1}{\gamma} = \dfrac{\alpha\beta + \beta\gamma + \gamma\alpha}{\alpha\beta\gamma} = \dfrac{3}{\dfrac{9}{2}} = \dfrac{2}{3}$.

classification.content: Sums and products of roots

stem.t: The polynomial $x^3 - 27x + c$, where $c > 0$, has a repeated zero.

sampleAnswer.t: A repeated zero is a zero of the derivative $3x^2 - 27$, so it is $x = \pm 3$. If it is $3$: $27 - 81 + c = 0$, so $c = 54$. If it is $-3$, $c = -54 < 0$.

classification.content: Multiple zeros of polynomials

sections.title: Section II
sections.instructions: Attempt Questions 11 to 14. Allow about 1 hour and 45 minutes for this section. Show relevant mathematical reasoning and/or calculations.

parts.label: (a)

prompt.t: Find the term independent of $x$ in the expansion of $\left(3 x + \dfrac{2}{x}\right)^{6}$.

sampleAnswer.t: The general term is $\dbinom{6}{k}\left(3 x\right)^{6 - k}\left(\dfrac{2}{x}\right)^{k}$, in which the power of $x$ is $(6 - k) - k$. This is zero when $k = 3$, so the term is $\dbinom{6}{3} \times 3^{3} \times 2^{3} = 4320$.

classification.content: Binomial expansion; term independent of x

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p10.py: SymPy expansion of (3x+2/x)^6, coefficient of x^0

prompt.t: Let $f(x) = (x - 4)^2 + 4$ for $x \ge 4$, and let $f^{-1}$ be its inverse function.
Find the coordinates of the points where the graphs of $y = f(x)$ and $y = f^{-1}(x)$ meet.

text.t: Explains why the graphs meet only on $y = x$, or solves $f(x) = x$ correctly

sampleAnswer.t: $f$ is increasing for $x \ge 4$. If $f(a) = b$ and $f^{-1}(a) = b$ then $f(b) = a$; if $a < b$ then $f(a) < f(b)$, that is, $b < a$, which is impossible, and similarly $a > b$ is impossible. So the graphs meet only on the line $y = x$, where $f(x) = x$: $x^2 - 9 x + 20 = 0$, so $(x - 4)(x - 5) = 0$. Both values satisfy $x \ge 4$, so the points are $(4, 4)$ and $(5, 5)$.

classification.content: Inverse functions; intersections with the inverse

parts.label: (c)

prompt.t: The points $A$, $B$ and $C$ are $(4, 2)$, $(2, 4)$ and $(1, 7)$.
Use vectors to find the coordinates of the point $P$ on the line $AB$ that is closest to $C$.

sampleAnswer.t: $\overrightarrow{AB} = -2\underset{\sim}{i} + 2\underset{\sim}{j}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC} = -3\underset{\sim}{i} + 5\underset{\sim}{j}$. The closest point is the foot of the perpendicular from $C$, $\overrightarrow{AP} = \dfrac{\overrightarrow{AC}\cdot\overrightarrow{AB}}{\left|\overrightarrow{AB}\right|^2}\overrightarrow{AB} = 2\overrightarrow{AB}$. So $P$ is $(0, 6)$.

classification.content: Vector projections; closest point on a line

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p10.py: SymPy minimisation of |A+t(B-A)-C|^2 along AB

parts.label: (d)

prompt.t: A ball is projected from a point $O$ on horizontal ground with speed $30$ m s$^{-1}$ at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal. It passes through the point that is 60 m horizontally from $O$ and $5$ m above the ground. Take $g = 10$ m s$^{-2}$, and assume the ball's position at time $t$ is $Vt\cos\theta\,\underset{\sim}{i} + \left(Vt\sin\theta - 5t^2\right)\underset{\sim}{j}$.
Find the two possible values of $\tan\theta$.

text.t: Solves the quadratic with a minor error
Obtains a correct quadratic equation in $\tan\theta$
Finds the time to reach the point

sampleAnswer.t: At horizontal distance $60$, $t = \dfrac{60}{30\cos\theta}$, so the height is $60\tan\theta - 20\sec^2\theta = 60\tan\theta - 20\left(1 + \tan^2\theta\right)$. Setting this equal to $5$ with $T = \tan\theta$: $\ 20T^2 - 60T + 25 = 0$. Its solutions are $T = \dfrac{1}{2}$ and $T = \dfrac{5}{2}$.

classification.content: Projectile motion; angles of projection through a given point

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p10.py: scan of theta in (0,pi/2) for height 5 m at 60 m horizontally from the stated position vector, roots refined by bisection: tan = 0.5, 2.5

prompt.t: Prove by mathematical induction that $10^{n+1} - 9n - 10$ is divisible by $81$ for all integers $n \ge 1$.

text.t: Verifies the base case and makes substantial progress with the inductive step

sampleAnswer.t: When $n = 1$ the expression is $81$, which is divisible by $81$. Assume that the expression for $n = k$ equals $81M$ for an integer $M$. Then for $n = k + 1$: $10^{k+2} - 9(k + 1) - 10 = 10\left(10^{k+1} - 9k - 10\right) + 81k + 81 = 810M + 81k + 81$, which is divisible by $81$. So the result holds for $n = k + 1$, and hence for all $n \ge 1$ by mathematical induction.

classification.content: Proof by induction; divisibility

parts.label: (a)

prompt.t: Find the least value of $\sin^2 x + 8\sin x\cos x - 4\cos^2 x$.

text.t: Writes the expression in the form $A + R\cos(2x - \alpha)$, or equivalent merit
Uses double-angle results to rewrite the expression

sampleAnswer.t: Using $\sin^2 x = \tfrac12(1 - \cos 2x)$, $\cos^2 x = \tfrac12(1 + \cos 2x)$ and $\sin x\cos x = \tfrac12\sin 2x$, the expression is $-\dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{5}{2}\cos 2x + 4\sin 2x$. Now $-\dfrac{5}{2}\cos 2x + 4\sin 2x = \dfrac{\sqrt{89}}{2}\cos(2x - \alpha)$ for a suitable angle $\alpha$, and $\cos(2x - \alpha)$ takes every value from $-1$ to $1$. So the least value is $- \dfrac{\sqrt{89}}{2} - \dfrac{3}{2}$.

classification.content: Double-angle results; auxiliary angle; extreme values

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p10.py: grid + golden-section minimum of the original expression over [0,2pi]: -6.2169905660

parts.label: (b)

prompt.t: The random variable $X$ has a binomial distribution with mean $\dfrac{15}{4}$. It is given that $P(X = 3) = P(X = 4)$.
Find the number of trials $n$.

sampleAnswer.t: Equating $\dbinom{n}{3}p^{3}(1 - p)^{n - 3}$ and $\dbinom{n}{4}p^{4}(1 - p)^{n - 4}$ gives $(n - 3)p = 4(1 - p)$, so $p = \dfrac{4}{n + 1}$. Then $np = \dfrac{4n}{n + 1} = \dfrac{15}{4}$, which gives $n = 15$.

classification.content: Binomial probabilities and mean

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p10.py: exact Fractions: mean 15/4 gives p=15/(4n); P(X=3)=P(X=4) holds only for n=15 over n=4..300

prompt.t: There are $m$ points on a line $L_1$ and $n$ points on a parallel line $L_2$. Every point on $L_1$ is joined to every point on $L_2$ by a straight segment, and no three segments pass through the same point between the lines. The diagram shows the case $m = 6$, $n = 7$.
Explain why the number of points between the lines where two segments cross is $\dbinom{m}{2}\dbinom{n}{2}$.

text.t: Recognises that two segments cross exactly when their endpoints are in opposite orders

sampleAnswer.t: Choose two points $A_1, A_2$ on $L_1$ and two points $B_1, B_2$ on $L_2$. Of the two ways to join them in pairs, exactly one pair of segments crosses between the lines. Every crossing comes from exactly one such choice, and there are $\dbinom{m}{2}\dbinom{n}{2}$ choices.

classification.content: Combinations; counting crossings; probability

parts.label: (ii)

prompt.t: Two of the segments in the diagram are chosen at random. Find the probability that they cross between the lines.

sampleAnswer.t: There are $42$ segments, so $\dbinom{42}{2} = 861$ pairs, and $\dbinom{6}{2}\dbinom{7}{2} = 315$ of them cross. The probability is $\dfrac{315}{861} = \dfrac{15}{41}$.

classification.content: Combinations; counting crossings; probability

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p10.py: all 861 pairs of the 42 segments classified by interleaved endpoints, exact Fraction

prompt.t: Show that when $m = n$, the probability that two segments chosen at random cross is $\dfrac{n - 1}{2(n + 1)}$.

text.t: Writes the probability using binomial coefficients

classification.content: Combinations; counting crossings; probability

parts.label: (iv)

prompt.t: Find the least value of $n$ for which this probability exceeds $\dfrac{2}{5}$.

sampleAnswer.t: $\dfrac{n - 1}{2(n + 1)} > \dfrac{2}{5} \iff 5(n - 1) > 4(n + 1) \iff n > 9$, so the least value is $n = 10$.

classification.content: Combinations; counting crossings; probability

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p10.py: all pairs of the n^2 segments enumerated for n=2..16: crossing probability first exceeds 2/5 at n=10

prompt.t: Two straight cushions on a billiard table meet at the origin $O$. One lies along the positive $x$-axis and the other along the line $\ell$ through $O$ in the direction of the unit vector $\hat{\underset{\sim}{u}} = \dfrac{1}{5}\left(4\underset{\sim}{i} + 3\underset{\sim}{j}\right)$, making an angle $\alpha$ with the $x$-axis. When the ball strikes a cushion, the component of its velocity along the cushion is unchanged and the component perpendicular to the cushion is reversed. A ball is struck from $A(4, 1)$ with velocity $\underset{\sim}{v} = 2\underset{\sim}{j}$. It rebounds from $\ell$ at $P$ and then from the $x$-axis at $Q$.

Show that the velocity of a ball with velocity $\underset{\sim}{w}$ just after it rebounds from $\ell$ is $\ 2\left(\underset{\sim}{w}\cdot\hat{\underset{\sim}{u}}\right)\hat{\underset{\sim}{u}} - \underset{\sim}{w}$.

text.t: Resolves $\underset{\sim}{w}$ into components along and perpendicular to $\hat{\underset{\sim}{u}}$

sampleAnswer.t: Write $\underset{\sim}{w} = \left(\underset{\sim}{w}\cdot\hat{\underset{\sim}{u}}\right)\hat{\underset{\sim}{u}} + \underset{\sim}{n}$, where $\underset{\sim}{n} = \underset{\sim}{w} - \left(\underset{\sim}{w}\cdot\hat{\underset{\sim}{u}}\right)\hat{\underset{\sim}{u}}$ is perpendicular to the cushion. After the rebound the velocity is $\left(\underset{\sim}{w}\cdot\hat{\underset{\sim}{u}}\right)\hat{\underset{\sim}{u}} - \underset{\sim}{n} = 2\left(\underset{\sim}{w}\cdot\hat{\underset{\sim}{u}}\right)\hat{\underset{\sim}{u}} - \underset{\sim}{w}$.

classification.content: Vectors; projections; reflection at a boundary; scalar product

parts.label: (ii)

prompt.t: Find the coordinates of $P$.

text.t: Writes the position of the ball at time $t$ and uses the equation of $\ell$

sampleAnswer.t: The ball is at $(4,\ 1 + 2t)$ at time $t$ and $\ell$ is $4y = 3x$. So $4(1 + 2t) = 3(4)$, giving $t = 1$ and $P = \left(4, 3\right)$.

classification.content: Vectors; projections; reflection at a boundary; scalar product

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p10.py: SymPy intersection of the path (4,1+2t), t>0, with the line through O along (4,3)

prompt.t: Let $\underset{\sim}{v}'$ be the velocity after the rebound at $Q$. Show that $\ \underset{\sim}{v}\cdot\underset{\sim}{v}' = |\underset{\sim}{v}|^2\cos 2\alpha\$ for every velocity $\underset{\sim}{v}$ for which the ball meets $\ell$ and then the $x$-axis, and hence find the angle between $\underset{\sim}{v}$ and $\underset{\sim}{v}'$ as an exact expression in inverse trigonometric form.

text.t: Provides a correct proof and the correct angle
Writes $\underset{\sim}{v}'$ in terms of the components of $\underset{\sim}{v}$

sampleAnswer.t: Let $\hat{\underset{\sim}{u}} = \cos\alpha\,\underset{\sim}{i} + \sin\alpha\,\underset{\sim}{j}$ and $\underset{\sim}{v} = a\underset{\sim}{i} + b\underset{\sim}{j}$. After the first rebound the velocity is $2(a\cos\alpha + b\sin\alpha)(\cos\alpha\,\underset{\sim}{i} + \sin\alpha\,\underset{\sim}{j}) - (a\underset{\sim}{i} + b\underset{\sim}{j})$, and the rebound at the $x$-axis reverses the $\underset{\sim}{j}$ component, so
\underset{\sim}{v}' = \left[2(a\cos\alpha + b\sin\alpha)\cos\alpha - a\right]\underset{\sim}{i} - \left[2(a\cos\alpha + b\sin\alpha)\sin\alpha - b\right]\underset{\sim}{j}.
Then
\underset{\sim}{v}\cdot\underset{\sim}{v}' = 2(a\cos\alpha + b\sin\alpha)(a\cos\alpha - b\sin\alpha) - a^2 + b^2
= a^2(2\cos^2\alpha - 1) + b^2(1 - 2\sin^2\alpha) = |\underset{\sim}{v}|^2\cos 2\alpha.

Since $|\underset{\sim}{v}'| = |\underset{\sim}{v}|$, the angle $\phi$ between them has $\cos\phi = \cos 2\alpha = \cos^2\alpha - \sin^2\alpha = \dfrac{7}{25}$, so $\phi = \cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{7}{25}\right)$, whatever the starting velocity.

classification.content: Vectors; projections; reflection at a boundary; scalar product

prompt.t: A dose of $350$ mg of a drug is swallowed at time $t = 0$ hours. Let $G$ mg be the amount in the gut and $B$ mg the amount in the bloodstream at time $t$. The drug moves from the gut to the blood, so that $\dfrac{dG}{dt} = -\dfrac{1}{5}G$, and the body removes it from the blood, so that $\ \dfrac{dB}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{5}G - \dfrac{1}{5}B$. Initially $G = 350$ and $B = 0$.

parts.label: (i)

prompt.t: Find $G$ as a function of $t$.

sampleAnswer.t: $\dfrac{1}{G}\dfrac{dG}{dt} = -\dfrac{1}{5}$, so $\ln G = -\dfrac{1}{5}t + C$, and $G = 350$ at $t = 0$ gives $G = 350e^{-\tfrac{1}{5}t}$.

classification.content: Differential equations; rates; maxima and points of inflection

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p10.py: RK4 integration of dG/dt=-G/5, G(0)=350 against the key at 8 times, max err < 1e-9

prompt.t: By considering $\dfrac{d}{dt}\left(Be^{\tfrac{1}{5}t}\right)$, show that $B = 70\,t\,e^{-\tfrac{1}{5}t}$.

text.t: Integrates to find $Be^{kt}$ (or equivalent) with the constant determined
Uses the product rule with the differential equation to simplify the derivative

sampleAnswer.t: $\dfrac{d}{dt}\left(Be^{\tfrac{1}{5}t}\right) = e^{\tfrac{1}{5}t}\left(\dfrac{dB}{dt} + \dfrac{1}{5}B\right) = e^{\tfrac{1}{5}t}\times \dfrac{1}{5}G = 70$, a constant. So $Be^{\tfrac{1}{5}t} = 70t + C$, and $B = 0$ at $t = 0$ gives $C = 0$, so $B = 70\,t\,e^{-\tfrac{1}{5}t}$.

classification.content: Differential equations; rates; maxima and points of inflection

prompt.t: Find the greatest amount of the drug in the bloodstream, and the time at which it occurs.

text.t: Provides the correct amount and time

sampleAnswer.t: $\dfrac{dB}{dt} = 70e^{-\tfrac{1}{5}t}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{5}t\right) = 0$ when $t = 5$, a maximum since $\dfrac{dB}{dt}$ changes from positive to negative there. The greatest amount is $B = \dfrac{350}{e}$ mg, at $t = 5$ hours.

classification.content: Differential equations; rates; maxima and points of inflection

prompt.t: The polynomial $P(x) = x^{3} + 4 x^{2} - 6 x + 3$ has zeros $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$. Find a polynomial with integer coefficients whose zeros are $\alpha + 2$, $\beta + 2$ and $\gamma + 2$.

text.t: Expresses $\alpha$ in terms of a new zero, or equivalent merit

sampleAnswer.t: If $u = \alpha + 2$ then $\alpha = u - 2$, so the new zeros satisfy $P(x - 2) = 0$: $x^{3} - 2 x^{2} - 10 x + 23 = 0$. So a suitable polynomial is $x^{3} - 2 x^{2} - 10 x + 23$ (any non-zero integer multiple is also correct).

classification.content: Polynomials; zeros of related polynomials

prompt.t: Use the substitution $t = \tan\dfrac{\theta}{2}$ to solve $7\cos\theta - \sin\theta = 5$ for $0 \le \theta \le 2\pi$. Give your answers in exact form.

sampleAnswer.t: With $\cos\theta = \dfrac{1 - t^2}{1 + t^2}$ and $\sin\theta = \dfrac{2t}{1 + t^2}$ the equation becomes $12 t^{2} + 2 t - 2 = 0$, that is, $2 \left(2 t + 1\right) \left(3 t - 1\right) = 0$, so $t = - \dfrac{1}{2}$ or $t = \dfrac{1}{3}$. Checking $\theta = \pi$ (where $t$ is undefined): $7\cos\pi = -7 \ne 5$, so it is not a solution. Since $0 \le \dfrac{\theta}{2} \le \pi$, the solutions are $\theta = 2\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)$ and $\theta = 2\pi - 2\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$.

classification.content: The t-formulae; solving trigonometric equations

prompt.t: The diagram shows the curve $y = 2\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{4}\right)$ for $0 \le x \le 4$. The region $S$ lies between the curve, the $x$-axis and the line $x = 4$. The region $T$ lies between the curve, the $y$-axis and the line $y = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

parts.label: (i)

prompt.t: Find the exact area of $S$.

text.t: Finds the area between the curve and the $y$-axis using the inverse function

sampleAnswer.t: The curve can be written $x = 4\tan\left(\dfrac{y}{2}\right)$. The area of $T$ is
\int_0^{\tfrac{\pi}{2}} 4\tan\left(\dfrac{y}{2}\right)dy = \left[-8\ln\left|\cos\dfrac{y}{2}\right|\right]_0^{\tfrac{\pi}{2}} = 8\ln\sqrt2,
and $S$ and $T$ together make a rectangle of area $2 \pi$, so the area of $S$ is $2 \pi - 4\ln 2$.

classification.content: Inverse trigonometric functions; areas and volumes of revolution

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p10.py: mpmath quadrature of the integral of 2atan(x/4) over [0,4] to 30 digits

parts.label: (ii)

prompt.t: The region $T$ is rotated about the $y$-axis. Find the exact volume of the solid formed.

text.t: Simplifies the integrand to a form that can be integrated
Writes a correct integral for the volume

sampleAnswer.t: $V = \pi\displaystyle\int_0^{\tfrac{\pi}{2}} 16\tan^2\left(\dfrac{y}{2}\right)dy = 16\pi\displaystyle\int_0^{\tfrac{\pi}{2}}\left(\sec^2\dfrac{y}{2} - 1\right)dy = 16\pi\left[2\tan\dfrac{y}{2} - y\right]_0^{\tfrac{\pi}{2}} = - 8 \pi^{2} + 32 \pi$.

classification.content: Inverse trigonometric functions; areas and volumes of revolution

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p10.py: mpmath quadrature pi*int_0^{pi/2}(4tan(y/2))^2 dy to 30 digits

parts.label: (iii)

prompt.t: The region $S$ is rotated about the $y$-axis. Find the exact volume of the solid formed.

text.t: Recognises that $S$ and $T$ together form a cylinder when rotated
Finds the volume of the cylinder of radius $4$

sampleAnswer.t: Rotating $S$ and $T$ together gives a cylinder of radius $4$ and height $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, with volume $8 \pi^{2}$. So the volume from $S$ is $8 \pi^{2} - \left(32 \pi - 8 \pi^{2}\right) = 16 \pi^{2} - 32 \pi$.

classification.content: Inverse trigonometric functions; areas and volumes of revolution

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p10.py: independent shell method 2pi*int_0^4 x*2atan(x/4) dx by mpmath to 30 digits
